newsitem.title: CHILE: Delay threatens Chile's Copec pulp plant.
newsitem.headline: Delay threatens Chile's Copec pulp plant.

text.p: Delays in carrying out studies on a waste water pipeline to the Pacific could put Chilean industrial firm Copec's huge wood pulp project near the southern town of Valdivia at risk, said a Copec director.

"There is no date (for finishing the studies), but the only thing one can say is that the longer they are delayed, then it is more obvious that the construction of the plant is at risk," Roberto Angelini told reporters.
The Valdivia plant, to be built by Copec's Celulosa Arauco y Constitucion pulp division, will cost $1 billion and produce 550,000 tonnes of wood pulp.
Chile's environment authorities approved the environmental impact study for the plant in May, but on condition that Copec installs a third plant to treat waste water.
Company officials have said that a third plant would be too expensive to run and the firm is studying building a duct which would enter the Pacific Ocean near the fishing port of Mehuin.
But the plan has run into stiff opposition from the port's fishermen and local ecologists.
The problems with environmental permits have already caused construction of the plant to be delayed by around a year.
Building work was originally due to have started by early 1997.
Copec, Chile's largest forestry firm, is 30 percent owned by New Zealand's Carter Holt Harvey.
